Rod has shipped 9 commits this morning hardening company-switch race conditions (#221-#226) and stale API key detection. Design partner deadline is tomorrow. Before inviting anyone in, we need to verify the fixed flows actually work end-to-end for a NEW user — not just Rod dogfooding.

End-to-end smoke test:

2. Company switch via UI → verify no stale data shown
3. API key rotation in test org → verify stale key warning surfaces
4. Deploy Gate required check enabled on a repo not in the PP org

All 5 flows complete without manual intervention or confusing state.

Comment on this issue with pass/fail per step + screenshots of any failures.

## Done When
All 5 flows verified ✅ OR blocking bugs filed + linked here.

## Context
Multi-tenant hardening is the #1 unannounced prerequisite for design partners. If a new user gets confused by company state during their first 5 minutes, they churn immediately.
References: master-plan.md → 'Partner must adopt organically (not hand-held through every step)'

### Concept
OpenClaw 2026.3 shipped with a bundled `copilot-proxy` plugin (VS Code Copilot Proxy bridge). 
This allows intercepting Copilot/IDE AI traffic locally.

### The Opportunity
Instead of waiting for code to hit the CI/CD Deploy Gate, we can apply Permission Protocol governance **directly inside the IDE**. 
- Catch unauthorized API calls or malicious suggestions *before* they are committed.
- Gating the prompt/suggestion loop itself.

### Execution & Marketing Plan
- **Do not execute or build yet.** We need to discuss the marketing angle and positioning first (e.g., "Governance prevents at the keystroke").
- We must define how the UX works for a developer. Does it pop up a PP receipt in the IDE?
title: Research: IDE-Level Governance via Copilot Proxy Bridge

body:
## Context

When the deploy-gate action sets the commit status on a PR, the `target_url` (details link) always points to the PP review/approval page:

```
https://app.permissionprotocol.com/review/<request-id>
```

This works well when the request is pending — clicking the check takes you to approve/reject. But after approval, the check shows "Successful in 0s" and clicking through lands on the approval page with nothing to do. Confusing for users who expect a summary/receipt view.

## Proposed Fix

After a deploy request is approved, update the commit status `target_url` to point to a **read-only receipt view** instead of the review page. Options:

1. **Existing receipt URL**: `/r/<receipt-id>` (already exists on the marketing site)
2. **App receipt view**: `/review/<id>?view=receipt` (read-only mode of the review page)
3. **Status badge**: A minimal "Approved ✓" page with receipt details

Option 2 is probably simplest — the review page already has the data, just needs a read-only state when the request is already resolved.

## Impact

Low priority / UX polish. But it's the kind of detail that makes the product feel polished vs. janky when users click around exploring what PP does.
title: Deploy-gate: set details URL to receipt view after approval
